evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Dinner is already in your fridge.' is a slogan; the lede ('Tell Pantrywise what you've got. It plans the week's dinners around it, and the shopping list is only what's missing.') makes the what clear. The 'who' (parents of picky kids) never appears in the first screen: it first shows up in the dark section 'Made for the table where somebody won't eat the green bits', about 2,700px down at 390. CTA 'Join the iPhone waitlist' has a clear object.
evidence.fit: Meets the explicit asks: waitlist goes to the supplied https://pantrywise.example/waitlist (all 4 links), the price section says free now with an unset family-plan price, and 'These are example dinners' covers the no-partner-recipes constraint. The picky-kid audience only gets a text section of four claims and nothing in the demo. As a parent with a picky eater I could not tell the tool what my kid refuses. The yellow fridge with masking-tape labels is memorable against grey recipe apps.
evidence.distinctiveness: The fridge-door frame (dark outline with a handle) and masking-tape ingredient labels with slight tilts are product-specific and recognisable without the logo. Below the hero it falls back to a generic stack: three numbered steps, a four-item text grid on navy, a plain FAQ list and a centred CTA band.
evidence.proof: 1440: the demo is in the first viewport, with chips, plan and 'Still need to buy' list all visible. Tapping 'Mince' swapped Tuesday to 'Build-your-own tacos' with 'From the house: mince, tortillas and cheddar'. Problem: 'Half a bag of spinach' is pre-ticked but none of the five default dinners uses it, which contradicts the page's own 'The half bag of spinach gets used on Tuesday' and undercuts the core 'uses what you have' promise. The example label sits at the bottom of the fridge, at y≈2200 at 390, well below the plan.
evidence.craft: Clean, consistent and confident at 1440/768/390: heavy sans headline, good contrast on the plan, tidy shopping note with tape. Probe shows 2 axe color-contrast nodes at 390/1440. The Shuffle link is small (0.9rem, 28px tall). The lower sections are plain and evenly spaced, with little hierarchy.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow and text ≥13.6px. Ingredient chips are 33–36px tall (under 44) and Shuffle is 28px. Tapping 'Mince' (y≈700) changes the plan at y≈1289 and the list at y≈1920, both off-screen, so a parent in the kitchen taps and sees nothing happen without scrolling. There is no nav or menu; the header has only a small 'Join the waitlist' button (38px tall).
evidence.honesty: No fabricated logos, users or quotes. But the copy states unbuilt specifics as fact: 'It takes about a minute the first time', 'sorted by aisle', 'Pantrywise remembers it between weeks', 'One tap moves the sauce... to the side', and 'Android is planned after that' (a roadmap the brief does not supply). The example label comes after the demo rather than at its top. The CTA note 'Free to use. iPhone first.' doesn't say what joining does until the closing band ('We'll email once when it's ready').
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: chips toggle with aria-pressed and Tab+Enter works (Enter on 'Mince' replanned Tuesday). Shuffle changes the week (with everything ticked: quesadillas/tuna melts/veggie fried rice...). Unticking all shows 'Tap a few things above to start.' and 'The list writes itself once there are dinners to plan.' Pasta alone gives an empty week with the same 'start' message even though one item is ticked. There is no reset. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Warm and specific in places ('somebody won't eat the green bits', 'used on Tuesday instead of thrown away on Sunday', 'No long back-stories above the method'). UK grocery words ('Mince', 'Tinned tomatoes', 'Fish fingers') feel off for a likely US iPhone audience. The dinner data has 'Tuna and sweetcorn pasta bake' with no sweetcorn among its ingredients. Short, with few repeats.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: slogan headline plus lede plus CTA, with the live fridge and the Mon/Tue plan and buy list visible: a believable artifact. 390: headline, lede, CTA and the top of the chip shelf, but no plan output in view. Neither width names the audience (picky kids, weeknights).

problems: The picky-eater audience the brief names gets no say in the demo and no mention in the first screen; a parent can't tell it what the kid refuses
The demo contradicts its own promise: pre-ticked 'Half a bag of spinach' is unused by every default dinner, while the copy claims the spinach 'gets used on Tuesday'

At 390, chips are ~34px and plan and list changes land 600–1,200px below the tapped chip, so feedback is invisible; unbuilt specifics ('about a minute', 'sorted by aisle', 'Android is planned') are stated as fact

hard_fail_flags.evidence: Borderline. The 'How a week gets planned' step 1 states a usage/performance number not supplied by the brief, as fact for an app with no users: 'It takes about a minute the first time, and Pantrywise remembers it between weeks.' It is not labelled as an example or a goal.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P001/A/index.html at any width, scroll to 'How a week gets planned', and read step 1 'Take stock' (index.html line 89).

evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Plan the week's dinners from the fridge, not the store.' and lead 'Pantrywise is a free iPhone app for parents of picky kids. Tick what's in your fridge and cupboard; it plans seven weeknight dinners around that and lists only what's missing.' cover what, for whom and the price. CTA 'Join the iPhone waitlist' with 'One email address, and we write when the app is ready' covers the next step. A stranger could repeat it.
evidence.fit: Both brief tensions get visible answers. The picky-kids audience gets 'The kids won't eat' vetoes inside the demo: 'Nothing spicy' swapped out Shakshuka, and 'Nothing mixed in' added a 'KIDS' line per dinner, e.g. 'plain omelette, spinach beside it'. Pricing appears beside the hero CTA and in a 'Free / Later' pair. Partner recipes are disclaimed in the sheet note. Weak spots: 'seven weeknight dinners' includes Sat/Sun, and the page is long (8,586px at 390) for a parent at 6pm.
evidence.distinctiveness: The fridge-shelf panel with drawn ingredient icons, the week plan as a paper sheet held by a tomato magnet, the kids' no-lists as magnet notes ('Max, 6'), Bookman-style serif display type and a phone-style shopping list all come from the kitchen. The section-head grid and FAQ accordion are familiar.
evidence.proof: 1440: shelf and plan rows Mon–Thu are in the first viewport, with status '7 dinners from 9 things on the shelf. 7 things to buy.' that matches the 7-item list. Changes propagate to the second list in the 'The list' section ('6 things for the week' after Nothing spicy). Labelled at the point of use ('A sample fridge. Tap what you have.'), with 'Example' captions on the step minis. Weaknesses: ticking 'Pasta' or 'No mushrooms' from the default changes nothing visible, and the picky section says 'the shopping list don't change' while the demo's list does change under 'Nothing spicy' (7→6 items).
evidence.craft: Deliberate type pairing (serif display, sans body), clear panel hierarchy, coloured USES/BUY keys and axe clean at 390/1440. 23 elements under 12px (the 11px uppercase 'USES'/'BUY'/'WON'T EAT' keys) are small but are labels, not body text. No defects seen at 1440/768/390 in any state I operated.
evidence.mobile: 390: no overflow. Chips are 44–54px tall and 'Put the sample back' is 45px. The Menu button opens a 5-item list, tapping 'Picky eaters' scrolled to #picky and closed it, and Escape closes it. Tapping 'Nothing mixed in' (Playwright scrolled to 737) flashed changed rows, with the status line and Monday row visible just below. Tapping a top shelf chip at y≈700 changes the status at y≈1420, off-screen. The buy list is at y≈2460, far down.
evidence.honesty: Examples are labelled where they appear ('A sample fridge', 'Example' captions, 'Example no-list', and 'Sample shelf, sample dinners... not recipes from partners'). The CTA says what happens before the click. Android: 'If that changes, this page will say so' (no invented roadmap). Footer: 'An iPhone app in development.' Two soft savings implications: 'most of the week is already paid for' and 'the picky kid costs nothing extra'. Unbuilt features are stated as fact ('in the order you walk the shop', 'counted in packets and tins').
evidence.interaction: Operated at all three widths. Checkbox chips toggle by tap/click and keyboard (Tab reached each chip, Space unticked cheddar → '10 things to buy' and quesadillas now 'BUY block of cheddar'). The vetoes work, reset restores the sample, and edge states are handled: all unticked gives 'Nothing on the shelf, so no plan yet.', and pasta only gives 'Only 2 dinners fit...'. The status uses role=status and changed rows flash. 'No mushrooms' has no visible effect from the default shelf. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific nouns from the kitchen ('Leftover rice', 'Half an onion', 'ticked off with one thumb while the other hand holds a basket', 'Picky eaters get a veto, not a lecture'). It speaks directly to recipe-app fatigue ('Recipe apps pick the dinners first and send you shopping for everything'). Buttons say what happens. There are small contradictions ('seven weeknight dinners' vs Sat/Sun; 'three piles' vs 'egg and peas on the side'), and the page is long and somewhat repetitive about the list.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific outcome, named audience, CTA with what-happens note, and the live shelf plus first four plan rows in view. 390: headline, audience-naming lead, CTA and its disclosure, and the top of 'On the shelf' with ticked chips, but no plan output visible without scrolling.

problems: At 390, plan and list feedback lands below the tapped shelf chips (status ~700px down, list ~1,700px down), and the page runs 8,586px, long for a parent at 6pm
Some controls look dead from the default sample: 'No mushrooms' and ticking 'Pasta' change nothing in the plan

Copy contradictions: 'seven weeknight dinners' includes Sat/Sun, and the picky section says the list doesn't change while the demo's list does; soft savings wording ('most of the week is already paid for')

reason: As the parent with a picky eater, B is the page where I can tell the tool what my kid won't eat and watch the week adapt, and it names me and says what joining does before I tap. A has the more striking fridge but leaves the picky-kid audience out of the demo and its sample contradicts its own spinach promise. If a fixed B still felt too long to finish on a phone at 6pm, or A added vetoes and fixed the unused spinach, I would reconsider.
